newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Di Tella talks of Falklands referendum.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Di Tella talks of Falklands referendum.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem's idea of sharing the Falkland Islands with Britain would require a constitutional referendum, Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella said in an interview published on Monday.

Menem recently declared the end of the government's policy of smoothing ties with Britain by separating the discussion over sovereignty of the islands from practical talks over oil and fishing rights.
Menem also proposed sharing the Falklands with Britain in December -- a proposal that London flatly rejected. Britain won a war with Argentina over the islands in 1982.
Di Tella told the Clarin newspaper that any shared sovereignty agreement with Britain would need a referendum to change the constitution but that no immediate vote is planned.

"It isn't that the government is thinking of such a thing," he said. "The point is that the 1994 constitution establishes that Argentina will not renounce full sovereignty over the Malvinas," he said using the Argentine name for the islands.
He added, "We will not reach any real agreement over the Malvinas that does not go through Congress or a referendum."
